title: Procurement and Perfusion-Decellularization of Porcine Vascularized Flaps in a Customized Perfusion Bioreactor
protocol: Prepare commercially available polypropylene snap-lock containers with watertight and airtight lids containing a silicone seal lining.
Drill two 1/4 in holes along the sides of the container.
Thread a short segment of L/S-16 platinum-coated silicone tubing through each hole.
Attach a male Luer connector at the internal portion of one tubing for inflow perfusate connection to tissue cannula.
Attach a female Luer connector at the external end of the inflow tubing to connect to a three-way stopcock.
Drill a single 1/4 in hole on the chamber lid.
Thread another short segment of L/S-16 platinum-coated silicone tubing through this hole for air vent.
Mix approximately 50 cm of L/S-16 platinum-coated silicone tubing to create inflow and outflow tubing.
Connect one end of the tubing to a yellow three-stop pump tubing.
Attach the other end of the tubing to a sterile 2 mL serological pipette.
Autoclave all components, including the chamber and tubing, in individually wrapped sterile packaging.
Prepare heparinized normal saline solution by diluting 1.5 mL of 1000 I.U./mL heparin stock solution in 100 mL of normal saline.
Slowly add 9 g of SDS powder to 18 L of autoclaved distilled-deionized water.
Use a large volume polypropylene carboy to accommodate the SDS solution.
Store the prepared 0.05% w/v SDS solution at room temperature when fully dissolved.
Reconstitute lyophilized DNase I to a stock concentration of 10 mg/mL with 5 mM CaCl2 in sterile dH2O.
Store the reconstituted DNase I solution as aliquots in a −20 °C freezer until ready for use.
On the day of usage, dilute DNase I stock 1:100 with Mg++(1.29 mM) and Ca++(1.98 mM) in sterile dH2O to a final concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Dilute 10x PBS stock 1:10 with sterile autoclaved water in a 5 L final volume in a polypropylene carboy.
Store the prepared 1x PBS solution at room temperature.
Prepare 1% antibiotics/antimycotics (A/A) in PBS by diluting 100x A/A 1:100 with sterile 1x PBS solution to a final volume of 1 L.
Store the prepared antibiotic and antimycotic solution at room temperature.
Add 3.13 mL of peracetic acid, 40 mL of ethanol, and 956 mL of sterile dH2O.
Bring the final volume to 1,000 mL and store the prepared peracetic acid/ethanol solution at room temperature.
Humanely euthanize the animal following the procurement of all flaps.
Fast pigs for at least 12 hours prior to surgery.
Sedate animals with ketamine (20 mg/kg intramuscular), atropine (0.04 mg/kg intramuscular), and midazolam (0.3 mg/kg intramuscular).
Induce anesthesia by inhalation of 5% isoflurane through a mask at a flow rate of 22-44 mL/kg/min for peripheral line insertion and intubation.
Maintain anesthesia with 0.5%-2% isoflurane at 22-44 mL/kg/min.
Check hemodynamic stability to ensure adequate depth of anesthesia.
Administer intravenous remifentanil (10-20 µg/kg/h) continuous rate infusion during surgery for analgesia.
Intubate the pig with an appropriate endotracheal tube (7-8 mm).
Connect the endotracheal tube to a ventilator set to a tidal volume of 8 mL/kg, PEEP of 5 cm H2O, FiO2 of 0.5, and respiratory rate of 14.
Insert a 22 G angiocath catheter into the ear vein.
Infuse warm 0.9% normal saline at 5-10 mL/kg/h throughout the procedure to maintain mean arterial pressure between 60 mmHg and 90 mmHg.
Continuously monitor heart rate, pulse oximetry, and end-tidal CO2.
Assess blood pressure and body temperature every 5 minutes.
Apply eye ointment to prevent ocular dryness while under anesthesia.
Prepare the entire surgical field with povidone-iodine.
Drape the surgical field with sterile towels.
Place the pig in the supine position.
Perform a xypho-umbilical laparotomy.
Mobilize the stomach cephalad to visualize the greater omentum.
Carefully place the omentum into the operative field.
Identify the gastro-epiploic vessels running along the greater curvature of the stomach.
Begin at the left aspect of the greater curvature where the left gastro-epiploic artery joins the splenic artery.
Using straight Stevens tenotomy scissors, skeletonize both the left gastro-epiploic artery and vein.
Ligate then divide both arteries and veins separately using surgical ties or clips.
Proceed along the greater curvature of the stomach from left to right.
Ligate and divide the short vascular branches arising from the omentum supplying the greater curvature of the stomach.
Continue the mobilization of the greater omentum until the junction of the right gastro-epiploic vessels and the gastroduodenal artery is encountered.
With clips or ties, ligate then divide the right gastroepiploic artery and veins separately to free the omental flap.
Divide the omentum along the middle into two halves.
Secure each half of the omentum with its respective gastro-epiploic artery and vein.
Cannulate the gastro-epiploic vessels with a 20-22 G cannula.
Tie the cannulated gastro-epiploic vessels securely with 3-0 silk ties.
Flush heparinized saline (15 I.U./mL) into the arterial cannula until clear venous outflow is observed.
Place the pig in a lateral decubitus position.
Shave the entire upper hindlimb bilaterally.
Prepare and drape using sterile procedures.
Mark the anterior boundary of the flap from the ASIS toward the lateral patella.
Identify the location of the pedicle approximately 6-8 cm from the ASIS along this line.
Mark a parallel posterior line approximately 8 cm to 10 cm from the anterior incision.
Mark the distal edge of the flap at the lateral patella.
Make an initial sharp incision in the skin at the distal margin near the patella using a scalpel.
Deepen the incision through subcutaneous tissue with cautery until fascia overlying rectus femoris is encountered.
Continue skin incisions toward the ASIS along previously marked boundaries.
Remove overlying skin component from underlying fascial layer.
Ligate or cauterize small perforator vessels to the skin.
Incise deep fascia at distal border of flap to allow muscle mobilization.
Mobilize fascia toward the ASIS while identifying vascular pedicle between muscles.
Dissect proximal aspect off the ASIS, protecting the vascular pedicle during dissection.
Trace pedicle toward deep femoral vessels and skeletonize lateral circumflex femoral artery and vein.
Ligate and divide both vessels where they join the deep femoral vessels.
Cannulate pedicle vessels individually with 20 G to 24 G angiocatheters, secured with silk ties.
Flush heparinized saline into flap arterial cannula until clear venous outflow is observed.
Place the pig on the operating table in the lateral decubitus position.
Position the dependent forelimb within the operative field.
Mark an approximate 3 cm x 3 cm skin flap square on the radial forearm.
Draw a line between the midpoint of the proximal flap margin and the antecubital fossa to denote the approximate course of the radial artery pedicle.
Confirm the arterial course with palpation.
Incise the skin using a scalpel at the distal aspect with a depth up to the antebrachial fascia.
Blunt dissect with tenotomy scissors until the distal radial artery and its two venae comitantes are encountered.
Ligate the artery and veins with surgical ties individually and divide.
Continue the skin incisions on the radial and ulnar margins of the marked skin square.
Mobilize the flap off the underlying radial bone with a surgical blade proceeding from a radial to ulnar direction while also raising the skin flap proximally toward the antecubital fossa.
Retract the space between the brachioradialis and flexor carpi radialis with a self-retaining retractor to expose the proximal radial artery and its venae comitantes.
Using tenotomy scissors, skeletonize the radial artery and venae comitantes proximally at the antecubital fossa.
Dissect the vessels from the surrounding fibrofatty tissues to achieve a pedicle length of approximately 5-6 cm.
Ligate and divide the artery and venae separately to free the radial forearm flap.
Cannulate the pedicle vessels with 20 G to 24 G angiocatheters, secured with 3-0 silk ties.
Flush heparinized saline (15 IU/mL) into the flap arterial cannula until a clear venous outflow is observed.
Keep flaps in cold saline at 4 °C until ready for decellularization.
Under deep isoflurane anesthesia, euthanize the animals with an intravenous injection of potassium chloride (100 mg/kg IV).
Confirm death by the absence of vital signs.
Assemble the tissue chamber with flaps under sterile conditions in a laminar flow biosafety cabinet.
Attach a three-way stopcock to both the inflow and outflow ports of the bioreactor.
Attach a 0.2 μm filter to the air vent port on the tissue chamber lid.
Prime the inflow tubing with sterile heparinized saline to eliminate air bubbles.
Place the flaps in the chamber.
Connect the flaps to the inflow tubing using the male Luer connector.
Screw the respective arterial cannula of each flap onto the male Luer and ensure a tight seal.
Flush heparinized saline through the stopcock to check that the Luer connection is without leaks and that the flaps can be perfused with evidence of venous outflow.
Close the tissue chamber lid.
Connect the inflow tubing with a yellow three-stop pump tubing to the inflow stopcock of the tissue chamber.
Attach an inline pressure sensor transducer to the inflow three-way stopcock for perfusion pressure monitoring.
Turn on the inflow peristaltic pump.
Set the tubing ID to 1.85 mm on the initial screen using the arrow key to proceed to the third tab.
Proceed to the second tab and set the perfusion rate as mode of delivery at 2 mL/min.
Ensure the direction of flow is correct as displayed on the screen.
Load the three-stop pump tubing to the peristaltic pump with a compatible cassette.
Repeat the procedure for the outflow peristaltic pump similar to above.
Set the outflow pump setting to rate at 4 mL/min.
Connect the outflow tubing with a yellow three-stop pump tubing to the outflow stopcock of the tissue chamber.
Load the three-stop pump tubing to the peristaltic pump with a compatible cassette.
Start the flow for both pumps by pressing the Power button.
Carry out all of the following steps for perfusion decellularization at room temperature.
Begin the perfusion of heparinized saline at 2 mL/min using a peristaltic pump.
Perfuse the flaps with heparinized saline in the tissue chamber for 15 min to remove any retained blood clots.
Aspirate residual saline in the tissue chamber.
Fill the tissue chamber with approximately 500 mL of SDS decellularization solution.
Transfer the inflow tubing to the SDS decellularization solution and perfuse the tissue at 2 mL/min.
Perfuse SDS for 2 days for omentum, 3 days for tensor fascia, and 5 days for radial forearm fascio-cutaneous flap.
Aspirate the existing SDS perfusate contained within the tissue chamber.
Transfer the inflow tubing into 1x PBS solution and perfuse the flaps for 1 day at 2 mL/min.
Remove the previous PBS solution and transfer the inflow tubing into DNase working solution.
Perfuse for 2 h at 2 mL/min.
Remove the DNase solution from the tissue chamber.
Place the inflow tubing in 1x PBS solution.
Submerge the tissues with 1x PBS solution in the chamber.
Perfuse 1x PBS solution for 1 day at 2 mL/min.
Sterilize the flaps with PAA/EtOH solution.
Transfer the inflow tubing into PAA/EtOH in dH2O solution and submerge the tissues in the same solution.
Perfuse PAA/EtOH at 2 mL/min for 3 h.
Disconnect the tubing from the three-way stopcocks after PAA/EtOH sterilization is complete.
Remove the flaps using aseptic technique and place the sterile instruments into PBS containing 1% antibiotics/antimycotics (A/A).
Immerse the flaps with PBS + 1% A/A for 15 min in two separate washes to fully neutralize residual acid.
Keep the flaps in PBS + 1% A/A at 4 °C until ready for recellularization.
Verify the sterility of the scaffolds by performing a swab culture on agar plates and examine for microbial growth.
Inoculate agar plates with swabs taken from each flap surface.
Culture the agar plates at 37 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Procure samples 3 mm to 10 mm in thickness from the flaps using a punch biopsy.
Fix biopsies in histological cassettes in normal buffered formalin for 24 h at room temperature.
Wash the biopsy cassettes in water or PBS for 15 min then place them in 70% ethanol until ready for tissue processing.
Embed biopsies in paraffin, allowing wax to solidify for 10-15 min on a cold plate.
Section paraffin blocks on a microtome to 5 µm thickness.
Stain the slides with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) according to standard protocols.
Image the tissue slides with light microscopy.
Obtain the dry weight of the tissue biopsies following overnight drying in an oven at 60 °C.
Digest samples in a papain extraction buffer at 65 °C overnight.
Centrifuge digested samples at 10,000 x g and transfer supernatant to a fresh microcentrifuge tube.
Assay the DNA content with a commercial DNA extraction kit as per the manufacturer's instructions.
